passages.text: Now the men of Israel had sworn an oath at Mizpah, saying, “Not one of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite.”
passages.sermon: The men of Israel gathered at Mizpah.\r\nThey made a solemn oath there.\r\nThey said, “None of us will give his daughter to a man from Benjamin as a wife.”
passages.original: וְאִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נִשְׁבַּ֥ע בַּמִּצְפָּ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לֹא־ יִתֵּ֥ן בִּתּ֛וֹ לְבִנְיָמִ֖ן לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: So the people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening, lifting up their voices and weeping bitterly.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel came to Bethel.
They sat there before God.
They stayed until evening.
They raised their voices.
They wept with great sorrow.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָעָם֙ בֵּֽית־ אֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֤שְׁבוּ שָׁם֙ עַד־ הָעֶ֔רֶב לִפְנֵ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ קוֹלָ֔ם וַיִּבְכּ֖וּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: “Why, O LORD God of Israel,” they cried out, “has this happened in Israel? Today in Israel one tribe is missing!”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke to God.
They cried out to the LORD, the God of Israel.
They said, “Why has this happened in Israel?”
They said, “Today, one tribe is missing from Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ לָמָ֗ה יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הָ֥יְתָה זֹּ֖את בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְהִפָּקֵ֥ד הַיּ֛וֹם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: The next day the people got up early, built an altar there, and presented burnt offerings and peace offerings.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel gathered at Bethel.
They came before God.
The next day, the people woke up early.
They built an altar at that place.
They offered burnt offerings on the altar.
They also offered peace offerings.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ הָעָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ־ שָׁ֖ם מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיַּעֲל֥וּ עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִֽים׃פ

passages.text: The Israelites asked, “Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come to the assembly before the LORD?” For they had taken a solemn oath that anyone who failed to come up before the LORD at Mizpah would surely be put to death.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke.
They asked a question.
They said, “Who did not come to the assembly before the LORD?”
They meant all the tribes of Israel.
The Israelites had made a solemn oath.
They swore about anyone who did not come before the LORD at Mizpah.
They said, “Anyone who does not come must be put to death.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־ עָלָ֧ה בַקָּהָ֛ל מִכָּל־ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּי֩ הַשְּׁבוּעָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֜ה הָיְתָ֗ה לַ֠אֲשֶׁר לֹא־ עָלָ֨ה אֶל־ יְהוָ֧ה הַמִּצְפָּ֛ה לֵאמֹ֖ר מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: And the Israelites grieved for their brothers, the Benjamites, and said, “Today a tribe is cut off from Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were the people of God.
The Israelites had twelve tribes.
Benjamin was one of these tribes.
The Israelites saw that Benjamin was almost destroyed.
The Israelites felt sorrow for the tribe of Benjamin.
The Israelites called the Benjamites their brothers.
The Israelites said, “Today, one tribe is cut off from Israel.”
passages.original: וַיִּנָּֽחֲמוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־ בִּנְיָמִ֖ן אָחִ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נִגְדַּ֥ע הַיּ֛וֹם שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָ֖ד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: What should we do about wives for the survivors, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them our daughters in marriage?”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke.
They asked a question about the Benjamite survivors.
They said, “What should we do for the men who remain alive?”
They needed to find wives for these survivors.
They had made a vow before the LORD.
They had sworn not to give their own daughters as wives to the Benjamites.
passages.original: מַה־ נַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם לַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים לְנָשִׁ֑ים וַאֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ נִשְׁבַּ֣עְנוּ בַֽיהוָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֛י תֵּת־ לָהֶ֥ם מִבְּנוֹתֵ֖ינוּ לְנָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: So they asked, “Which one of the tribes of Israel failed to come up before the LORD at Mizpah?” And, in fact, no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp for the assembly.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites gathered together.
They spoke to each other.
They asked a question.
They said, “Is there any tribe of Israel that did not come up before the LORD at Mizpah?”
They looked for those who were missing.
They discovered something.
No one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp.
No person from Jabesh-gilead joined the assembly.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֗י אֶחָד֙ מִשִּׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ עָלָ֥ה אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹ֣א בָא־ אִ֧ישׁ אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה מִיָּבֵ֥ישׁ גִּלְעָ֖ד אֶל־ הַקָּהָֽל׃

passages.text: For when the people were counted, none of the residents of Jabesh-gilead were there.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel gathered together.
They counted everyone present.
They looked for people from every tribe.
They checked for residents of Jabesh-gilead.
They found no one from Jabesh-gilead among them.
passages.original: וַיִּתְפָּקֵ֖ד הָעָ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין־ שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ מִיּוֹשְׁבֵ֖י יָבֵ֥שׁ גִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: So the congregation sent 12,000 of their most valiant men and commanded them: “Go and put to the sword those living in Jabesh-gilead, including women and children.
passages.sermon:
The congregation of Israel gathered together.
They chose twelve thousand strong and brave men.
They sent these men on a mission.
They gave them a command.
They said, “Go to Jabesh-gilead.
Strike down all who live there with the sword.
Kill the men.
Kill the women.
Kill the children.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלְחוּ־ שָׁ֣ם הָעֵדָ֗ה שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וַיְצַוּ֨וּ אוֹתָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר לְ֠כוּ וְהִכִּיתֶ֞ם אֶת־ יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יָבֵ֤שׁ גִּלְעָד֙ לְפִי־ חֶ֔רֶב וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּֽף׃

passages.text: This is what you are to do: Devote to destruction every male, as well as every female who has had relations with a man.”
passages.sermon:
The leaders gave a command to the soldiers.
They said, “You must do this.”
Kill every male among the people of Jabesh-gilead.
Kill every woman who has had relations with a man.
Do not spare them.
passages.original: וְזֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ כָּל־ זָכָ֗ר וְכָל־ אִשָּׁ֛ה יֹדַ֥עַת מִשְׁכַּב־ זָכָ֖ר תַּחֲרִֽימוּ׃

passages.text: So they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young women who had not had relations with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites searched among the people of Jabesh-gilead.
They found four hundred young women there.
These women were virgins.
They had not had relations with any man.
The Israelites took these four hundred young women.
They brought them to their camp at Shiloh.
Shiloh was in the land of Canaan.
passages.original: וַֽיִּמְצְא֞וּ מִיּוֹשְׁבֵ֣י׀ יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֗ד אַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־ יָדְעָ֛ה אִ֖ישׁ לְמִשְׁכַּ֣ב זָכָ֑ר וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ אוֹתָ֤ם אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ שִׁלֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃ס

passages.text: Then the whole congregation sent a message of peace to the Benjamites who were at the rock of Rimmon.
passages.sermon:
The whole congregation acted together.
They sent a message.
They sent this message to the Benjamites.
The Benjamites were at the rock of Rimmon.
The congregation spoke to them.
They offered them peace.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַֽיְדַבְּרוּ֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּסֶ֣לַע רִמּ֑וֹן וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: And at that time the Benjamites returned and were given the women who were spared from Jabesh-gilead. But there were not enough women for all of them.
passages.sermon:
The Benjamites were a tribe of Israel.
At that time, the Benjamites returned.
The people gave the Benjamites the women who survived from Jabesh-gilead.
These women came from Jabesh-gilead.
The people had spared these women.
There were not enough women for all the Benjamites.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שָׁב בִּנְיָמִן֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִיּ֔וּ מִנְּשֵׁ֖י יָבֵ֣שׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד וְלֹֽא־ מָצְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: The people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a void in the tribes of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel felt sorrow for the tribe of Benjamin.
The LORD had caused a gap among the tribes of Israel.
Benjamin had lost many people.
The people mourned this loss.
passages.original: וְהָעָ֥ם נִחָ֖ם לְבִנְיָמִ֑ן כִּֽי־ עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה פֶּ֖רֶץ בְּשִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Then the elders of the congregation said, “What should we do about wives for those who remain, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed?”
passages.sermon:
The elders of the congregation spoke.
They asked a question.
They said, “What should we do for the men who remain?”
They meant the men of the tribe of Benjamin.
They needed wives for these men.
They explained the problem.
They said, “The women of Benjamin have been destroyed.”
There were no wives left for the surviving men of Benjamin.
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְר֨וּ זִקְנֵ֣י הָעֵדָ֔ה מַה־ נַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים לְנָשִׁ֑ים כִּֽי־ נִשְׁמְדָ֥ה מִבִּנְיָמִ֖ן אִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: They added, “There must be heirs for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe of Israel will not be wiped out.
passages.sermon:
The elders of the congregation spoke.
They said there must be heirs for the survivors of Benjamin.
Benjamin is one of the tribes of Israel.
A tribe of Israel must not be wiped out.
Benjamin must not disappear from Israel.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ יְרֻשַּׁ֥ת פְּלֵיטָ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִ֑ן וְלֹֽא־ יִמָּחֶ֥ה שֵׁ֖בֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: But we cannot give them our daughters as wives.” For the Israelites had sworn, “Cursed is he who gives a wife to a Benjamite.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of Israel spoke.
They said, “We cannot give our daughters as wives to the men of Benjamin.
The Israelites made a vow.
They swore, ‘Cursed is anyone who gives a wife to a Benjamite.’”
passages.original: וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל לָתֵת־ לָהֶ֥ם נָשִׁ֖ים מִבְּנוֹתֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־ נִשְׁבְּע֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָר֕וּר נֹתֵ֥ן אִשָּׁ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִֽן׃ס

passages.text: “But look,” they said, “there is a yearly feast to the LORD in Shiloh, which is north of Bethel east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Israel spoke to the people.
They said, “There is a yearly feast to the LORD in Shiloh.”
Shiloh is north of Bethel.
Shiloh is east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem.
Shiloh is south of Lebonah.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ הִנֵּה֩ חַג־ יְהוָ֨ה בְּשִׁל֜וֹ מִיָּמִ֣ים׀ יָמִ֗ימָה אֲשֶׁ֞ר מִצְּפ֤וֹנָה לְבֵֽית־ אֵל֙ מִזְרְחָ֣ה הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ לִמְסִלָּ֔ה הָעֹלָ֥ה מִבֵּֽית־ אֵ֖ל שְׁכֶ֑מָה וּמִנֶּ֖גֶב לִלְבוֹנָֽה׃

passages.text: So they commanded the Benjamites: “Go, hide in the vineyards and watch. When you see the daughters of Shiloh come out to perform their dances, each of you is to come out of the vineyards, catch for himself a wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
passages.sermon:
The leaders spoke to the men of the tribe of Benjamin.
They gave them instructions.
They said, “Go now.
Hide yourselves in the vineyards.
Watch carefully.
You will see the daughters of Shiloh come out.
They will come to dance in the dances.
When you see them, come out quickly from the vineyards.
Each of you must seize a wife for himself.
Take her from the daughters of Shiloh.
Then go back to the land of Benjamin.”
passages.original: וַיְצַו אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכ֖וּ וַאֲרַבְתֶּ֥ם בַּכְּרָמִֽים׃ וּרְאִיתֶ֗ם וְ֠הִנֵּה אִם־ יֵ֨צְא֥וּ בְנוֹת־ שִׁילוֹ֮ לָח֣וּל בַּמְּחֹלוֹת֒ וִֽיצָאתֶם֙ מִן־ הַכְּרָמִ֔ים וַחֲטַפְתֶּ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם אִ֥ישׁ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מִבְּנ֣וֹת שִׁיל֑וֹ וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֖ם אֶ֥רֶץ בִּנְיָמִֽן׃

passages.text: When their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we will tell them, ‘Do us a favor by helping them, since we did not get wives for each of them in the war. Since you did not actually give them your daughters, you have no guilt.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Israel spoke to the people.
They gave instructions about the Benjamites.
They said, “If the fathers or brothers of the women come to us,
and they complain about what happened,
we will answer them.
We will say, ‘Please show kindness to the Benjamites.
Help them in this matter.
We did not get wives for them during the war.
You did not give your daughters to them yourselves.
You are not guilty in this situation.’”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֡ה כִּֽי־ יָבֹ֣אוּ אֲבוֹתָם֩ א֨וֹ אֲחֵיהֶ֜ם לָרוֹב אֵלֵ֗ינוּ וְאָמַ֤רְנוּ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ חָנּ֣וּנוּ אוֹתָ֔ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָקַ֛חְנוּ אִ֥ישׁ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֣י לֹ֥א אַתֶּ֛ם נְתַתֶּ֥ם לָהֶ֖ם כָּעֵ֥ת תֶּאְשָֽׁמוּ׃ס

passages.text: The Benjamites did as instructed and carried away the number of women they needed from the dancers they caught. They went back to their own inheritance, rebuilt their cities, and settled in them.
passages.sermon:
The Benjamites were a tribe of Israel.
The Benjamites followed the instructions they received.
They took as many women as they needed.
They took these women from the dancers they had caught.
The Benjamites left with the women.
They returned to their own land.
They rebuilt their cities.
They lived in those cities.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ נָשִׁים֙ לְמִסְפָּרָ֔ם מִן־ הַמְּחֹלְל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּזָ֑לוּ וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ וַיָּשׁ֙וּבוּ֙ אֶל־ נַ֣חֲלָתָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ֙ אֶת־ הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And at that time, each of the Israelites returned from there to his own tribe and clan, each to his own inheritance.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites had no king at that time.
Each Israelite belonged to a tribe and a family.
Each man left that place.
Each man went back to his own tribe.
Each man went back to his own family.
Each man returned to his own land.
passages.original: וַיִּתְהַלְּכ֨וּ מִשָּׁ֤ם בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אִ֥ישׁ לְשִׁבְט֖וֹ וּלְמִשְׁפַּחְתּ֑וֹ וַיֵּצְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ לְנַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
passages.sermon:
At that time, Israel had no king.
No one ruled over the people.
Each person did what he thought was right.
Everyone followed his own way.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֛ישׁ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
